title: Zenith GPU Systems - Partner intro & discovery
meeting_header: Date: 2025-07-22 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45 minutes | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Hannah Cho (Redwood Solutions), Rajiv Menon (Zenith Head of Partnerships), Sofia Alvarez (Zenith SA), Tom Becker (Zenith BD)
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood Inference and Zenith GPU Systems. Discussed partnership models (reference architecture for co-selling, joint benchmark program), integration touchpoints (APIs, deployment reference for Dedicated & Private), target customer segments (cloud service providers & SI customers), and action items to run a pilot benchmark on Zenith hardware. Security and resale/partner commercial model briefly covered. Next step: share partner deck, schedule technical deep-dive and set up testbed access.
topics: Technical integration: drivers, AMIs, testbed and benchmark plan
Target go-to-market segments and joint customers
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we're excited to meet the Zenith team. Quick audio check?
[00:08] Rajiv (Zenith): Yeah good here - thanks Maya. Sofia and Tom are on too.
[00:15] Liam (Redwood SE): Great. Quick agenda: intro, partnership models, technical touchpoints, then next steps. Sound good?
[00:22] Tom (Zenith): Yep, go for it.
[00:30] Maya: I'll kick us off — quick about Redwood: developer-first inference platform, hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC / on-prem) — we help teams make inference predictable and cheaper.
[00:45] Rajiv: Nice. We're Zenith GPU Systems — hardware + cluster integration for hyperscale and enterprise SI partners. We're exploring partnerships for inference stack partners for co-sell and validated configs.
[00:58] Hannah (Redwood): We've worked with a few OEMs and cloud partners; common models are validated stacks, reference AMIs/containers, and benchmarking programs.
[01:12] Sofia: Curious about what a 'validated stack' looks like — are you providing kernels, or is that on the partner?
[01:20] Liam: Good question. For Redwood, we provide inference runtime + optimized kernels; integration points for partners are drivers, CUDA/ROCm compatibility, and sometimes packaging optimized AMIs/containers. We usually collaborate on kernel tuning per device family.
[01:40] Rajiv: Does Redwood do quantization and mixed precision tuning on your side? We have customers who care about 4-bit and 8-bit profiles.
[01:50] Maya: Yes, Redwood Optimize gives recommendations on quantization profiles; our runtime supports quantization-friendly paths. For partner pilots we usually test multiple profiles to measure latency and quality tradeoffs.
[02:05] Tom: Sounds promising. Main question from BD — what's the commercial model for partners? Referral, reseller, or integration fee?
[02:14] Rajiv: Also — do you have an MOU for channel partnership?
[02:20] Maya: We have multiple partnership motions. Typically: co-sell/referral for cloud partners, validated-engineering partnerships with joint benchmarks, and reseller/licensing for dedicated/private installs. We can share a partner deck + template MOU.
[02:36] Sofia: On security — our enterprise customers demand KMS and audit logs; are those part of Redwood Private?
[02:44] Liam: Redwood Private includes integrations with KMS/HSM, audit logs, and customer-managed networking (V-P-C). For hosted we offer contract SLAs, but private is where customers get KMS/EKM and full auditability.
[02:58] Rajiv: When you say V-P-C, do you mean single-tenant or just VPC peering? Some SIs want air-gapped options.
[03:06] Hannah: Both — we offer private deployment options and on-prem packages for regulated or air-gapped environments.
[03:15] Tom: For the pilot, what kind of access will you need to our hardware? Root? A node?
[03:22] Liam: Preferably a testbed node with sudo to install drivers/containers; we can also bring a reference container if you prefer. For benchmarks we need sample models, KV cache warmups, and steady-state token profiles.
[03:36] Rajiv: Ok — we can provision a 1-2 node test cluster; will confirm.
[03:42] Maya: Great. On the benchmarks — typical metrics: p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory, and cost per 1M tokens equivalently.
[03:54] Sofia: Do you have an example benchmark report?
[04:00] Liam: Yes, we'll share a benchmarking spreadsheet and a runbook. We'll include sequences (short chat workloads and long-form generation) and both batch and streaming tests.
[04:15] Rajiv: Competitors we see doing similar: CoreWeave, Lambda Labs, NVIDIA Cloud. What's Redwood's differentiator on the partnership side?
[04:25] Maya: We focus on production-grade serving with unified API across hosted, dedicated and private; operational tooling, rollout capabilities, and cost-aware controls like batching and KV caching — the goal is easier productization for customers.
[04:40] Tom: Do you have any reference partners in the GPU vendor space?
[04:45] Hannah: We've done pilot integrations with two OEMs and a cloud partner last year; we can share anonymized outcomes.
[04:52] [06:02] Rajiv: (unclear) Sorry there was a brief lag — did you say you support ROCm for AMD GPUs?
[06:10] Liam: We do support ROCm for most of our stack; some advanced kernels are CUDA-first but we have ongoing work for ROCm parity.
[06:22] Sofia: For SIs we often need infra-as-code templates. Does Redwood provide Terraform modules or cloudformation?
[06:30] Maya: We have Terraform modules for Dedicated and docs for Private deployments; for partners we can provide example IaC templates.
[06:40] Tom: Good. On the commercial ask: our BD wants a partner margin model — how does Redwood handle reseller margins?
[06:48] Maya: Typical reseller discounts are handled via partner contracts; for pilots we do co-funded benchmark options. We'll include sample commercial tiers in the partner deck.
[06:58] Rajiv: Technical: latency requirements for enterprise customers tend to be sub-100ms p95 for chat loads. Has Redwood achieved that on your Dedicated offering?
[07:08] Liam: Depends on model & sequence length; with batching and optimized kernels we've seen p95 sub-100ms for smaller chat models (2-7B) on Dedicated pools. For larger models latency increases — we usually suggest a model-family strategy.
[07:24] Sofia: If we integrate, will Redwood route traffic to our hardware or do customers always hit Redwood Hosted?
[07:32] Maya: We can route based on policy — routing by latency/cost/region — so traffic can land on Zenith-hosted Dedicated capacity if configured.
[07:42] Tom: Any requirements on telemetry and tracing? Our customers want distributed tracing.
[07:48] Liam: Redwood Console offers tracing hooks and per-route dashboards; we expose traces and token-level cost breakdowns. We can integrate tracing with partner observability if needed.
[08:00] Rajiv: Great. A couple of follow-ups from our infra team — do you require kernel-level changes to the firmware or just driver level?
[08:08] Liam: Mostly driver and runtime-level tuning; kernel patches are rare. For some silicon-specific optimizations we may need microcode or driver updates, but we try to avoid kernel modifications.
[08:20] Maya: Let's talk pilot scope — propose: a 2-node Zenith testbed, run 3 model families (small chat model, medium instruction model, larger LLM), measure latency, throughput, and cost; target 3-week engagement.
[08:35] Rajiv: That timeline sounds doable. Who would run the benchmark runs?
[08:40] Liam: Redwood SEs with partner support; Zenith to provide nodes and access. We'll collaborate on runbook and dataset.
[08:48] Tom: For licensing, do you have a developer trial or partner sandbox?
[08:53] Maya: We offer trial credits on Hosted and partner testbeds for Dedicated pilots.
[09:00] Sofia: On compliance: SOC 2 and ISO?
[09:04] Hannah: Redwood is SOC 2 compliant; we're working on ISO attestations. We'll share security docs.
[09:12] Rajiv: Can you share an anonymized benchmark from a similar partner?
[09:16] Liam: Yes — I'll attach a sanitized benchmark and the runbook.
[09:20] Maya: We'll also share the partner playbook: co-sell motions, lead handoff, and revenue splits.
[09:28] [12:02] Tom: A question about edge cases — air-gapped installs for government customers, do you support air-gap?
[12:10] Hannah: We provide on-prem package for air-gapped environments; there is an extra validation step and ops support.
[12:20] Rajiv: Ok. What integration work is required for billing/mediation if we resell?
[12:26] Maya: For reseller deals we can integrate billing via invoice, and for more advanced partnerships we can integrate marketplace billing. We'll detail this in the deck.
[12:36] Sofia: Any required legal terms up front? NDA?
[12:40] Maya: We can sign an NDA; we have a partner MOU template too.
[12:46] Rajiv: Good.
[12:50] Liam: Quick technical note — for benchmarking long context workloads we measure KV cache hit rates; we recommend tests with both warm and cold caches.
[12:58] Tom: Makes sense.
[13:04] Maya: I'll summarize action items at the end. Anything else on the technical side?
[13:10] Sofia: On the model side — do you prefer open models or can we run private/custom models?
[13:16] Liam: Both. We support open models and customers' private models; for private models we handle versioning and private keys and the same runtime.
[13:24] Rajiv: For a joint go-to-market, we can target telco and enterprise SI customers first. Those are our top segments.
[13:32] Maya: That matches a lot of our customers too.
[13:36] [20:00] (brief pause; background noise)
[20:10] Tom: One operational question — what SLOs do you commit to for Dedicated?
[20:16] Maya: We have SLA-backed uptime and latency targets for Dedicated engagements; specifics depend on contract tier. We'll share SLA examples.
[20:26] Rajiv: Regarding observability retention — some customers want 12 months. Is that an add-on?
[20:32] Hannah: We have add-ons for extended observability retention and enhanced audit logs.
[20:40] Sofia: Ok. On partner integration — is there a sandbox API for us to hit?
[20:45] Liam: Yes, we provide sandbox endpoints and credentials for pilots.
[20:50] Rajiv: Good.
[20:54] Maya: Let's call out potential blockers: firmware/driver mismatch, NDA timeline, and scheduling the testbed access.
[21:02] Tom: Agreed.
[21:08] Rajiv: Do you have a preference on who drafts the MOU?
[21:12] Maya: We can draft an initial MOU and send to you for review.
[21:17] Sofia: Perfect.
[21:20] Maya: ok, quick recap of next steps and action items.
[21:24] [35:00] Maya: Action items: Maya to send partner deck and MOU template; Liam to share benchmark runbook and sample report; Zenith (Rajiv/Sofia) to provision 2-node test cluster creds; set up technical deep dive next week.
[35:18] Rajiv: We'll aim to provision by Friday.
[35:22] Tom: We'll review the deck and follow up on commercial models.
[35:28] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites and links.
[35:34] Sofia: Thanks all.
[35:38] Liam: Thanks, goodbye.
[35:40] Rajiv: Bye.
next_steps: Maya to send partner deck and sample MOU (partner playbook)
Liam to share benchmark runbook and sanitized benchmark report
Zenith to provision 2-node test cluster and share access by 2025-07-25
Schedule technical deep-dive (SE-led) for week of 2025-07-28

Liam O'Connor - Provide benchmark runbook, sample report, and sandbox creds - due 2025-07-23
